title: PII Redaction
subtitle: Black out private data before an AI sees it
warning: This is a simplified teaching example, not a production security tool. Real systems need defense in depth, not a single regex filter.
intro_1: Imagine you want a friend to help you with a letter from your bank. Before you hand it over, you take a thick black marker and cross out your account number, your email and anything else private. Your friend can still help — they just can't see the secret bits.
intro_2: AI works the same way. Documents people paste into an AI often contain personal data — names, ID numbers, card numbers, emails. Before a document goes to an AI, a program can redact it: find the private bits and black them out. This demo does that with simple patterns, then checks its own work to show what the marker missed.
fake_note: All the personal data here is made up: ID numbers start with 000 (real ones never do), the card numbers are standard test numbers, and every email ends in example.com.

explain: The tidy cases are caught: the ID number with dashes, both card numbers, both normal emails. But names look like any other words to a pattern, and data written in an unusual way (with spaces, or spelled out in words) slips straight through. 5 out of 11 is not safe — that's the lesson.
try_help: Type a made-up sentence with an ID number, card number or email in it, and watch it get blacked out as you type. Then write the same thing a different way and see if it slips through.
try_placeholder: e.g. Call Sam on 000-99-8888 or email sam@example.com
try_example: Card 4111 1111 1111 1111, ID 000-11-2222, email me at sam@example.com — or sam at example dot com.
try_warning: Only ever use made-up details. Nothing you type leaves your browser — there is no server.
